# 📘 Overview

<div class="box">
This repository is organized to support a reproducible, maintainable and scalable Natural Language Query (NLQ) prototype for RVAT data. In addition to the Shiny application, the repository contains infrastructure for benchmark execution, model selection, manual EM/EX evaluation, performance aggregation, dataset validation, statistical analysis and reproducible research reporting.
</div>

# 🏗️ RVAT NLQ Architecture Overview

<details open>
<summary><b>⚙️ Core Logic (R/)</b></summary>
<br>
<div class="box">
The <code>R/</code> folder contains the authoritative production implementation of the RVAT NLQ system. These components power the Shiny application and are reused by the benchmark execution workflow to ensure that experimental observations are generated using the same query execution, logging and model configuration logic as the production environment.
<br>


- **01_db_connection.R**
  - Establishes database connectivity and provides access to the active RVAT database context.
  
- **02_ollama_config.R**
  - Configures Ollama models, prompt templates, model parameters and context construction.
  
- **03_query_execution.R**
  - Executes the core Natural Language → SQL → Database workflow and retrieves query results.
  
- **04_logging_pipeline.R**
  - Captures execution telemetry, generated SQL, token usage, execution status, errors and VES metrics.
  
- **05_shiny_ui.R**
  - Defines the user interface layout, controls and presentation components.
  
- **06_shiny_server.R**
  - Coordinates user interactions and integrates the NLQ pipeline with the Shiny application.

  
<br>
<b>Execution flow:</b>
<br>
User Query / Benchmark Question<br>
↓<br>
Database Context (01_db_connection.R)<br>
↓<br>
Prompt Construction & Model Configuration (02_ollama_config.R)<br>
↓<br>
SQL Generation (LLM)<br>
↓<br>
Query Execution (03_query_execution.R)<br>
↓<br>
Logging & Telemetry Collection (04_logging_pipeline.R)<br>
↓<br>
Results<br>
↓<br>
Shiny Interface (05_shiny_ui.R + 06_shiny_server.R)<br>
or<br>
Benchmark Data Capture (32_run_raw_data_capture.R)
</div>
</details>


<details>
<summary><b>🧪 Research Pipeline (scripts/)</b></summary>
<br>
<div class="box">
The <code>scripts/</code> folder contains the benchmarking, evaluation and analysis workflows used to assess Large Language Models (LLM's) within the RVAT NLQ environment.

Unlike the <code>R/</code> folder, which contains the authoritative production implementation, the research pipeline orchestrates data collection, manual evaluation, validation and statistical analysis around the production system. Benchmark executions deliberately reuse the production database, model configuration, query execution and logging components to ensure that experimental observations reflect production behaviour.
<br>

<br>
<b>Research Workflow</b>
<br>

<b>1. Model Selection & Triage</b>
<br>
Scripts:
<code>20_select_model_guide.R</code>,
<code>30_run_triage_llm.R</code>,
<code>31_run_triage_executor.R</code>
<br>

Purpose:
Identify and benchmark candidate LLM's before inclusion in the experimental workflow.
<br><br>

<b>2. Benchmark Data Collection</b>
<br>
Scripts:
<code>32_run_raw_data_capture.R</code>,
<code>33_prepare_evaluation_data.R</code>,
<code>34_analyse_evaluation.R</code>
<br>

Purpose:
Execute benchmark questions through the production pipeline, prepare evaluation datasets and construct a validated execution-level master dataset.
<br><br>

<b>3. Performance Analysis & Validation</b>
<br>
Scripts:
<code>35_analyse_performance.R</code>,
<code>36_A_master_dataset_verification.R</code>
<br>

Purpose:
Generate analytical datasets and verify completeness, consistency and statistical readiness.
<br><br>

<b>4. Visual Analytics</b>
<br>
Scripts:
<code>36_B_visualise_EM_EX.R</code>,
<code>36_C_visualise_EM_EX_per_model.R</code>,
<code>38_A_VES_overall.R</code>,
<code>38_B_VES_per_model.R</code>,
<code>40_A_SQL_generation_quality.R</code>
<br>

Purpose:
Produce publication-ready figures used to interpret benchmark performance.
<br><br>

<b>5. Statistical Inference</b>
<br>
Scripts:
<code>37_A_EX_significance_tests.R</code>,
<code>37_B_EX_performance_and_significance.R</code>,
<code>39_A_VES_significance_tests.R</code>,
<code>39_B_VES_performance_and_significance.R</code>
<br>

Purpose:
Determine whether observed performance differences between LLM's are statistically significant.
<br><br>

<b>Research Workflow</b>
<br>
Model Selection & Triage<br>
↓<br>
Benchmark Execution<br>
↓<br>
Raw Data Capture<br>
↓<br>
Manual EM / EX Evaluation<br>
↓<br>
Master Dataset Construction<br>
↓<br>
Performance Analysis<br>
↓<br>
Dataset Validation<br>
↓<br>
Visualisation & Statistical Testing<br>
↓<br>
Research Reporting
<br>
<br>

<b>Benchmark Metrics</b>
<br>

<b>Exact Match (EM)</b><br>
Manual assessment of whether the generated SQL corresponds to the benchmark reference query.
<br>

<b>Execution Match (EX)</b><br>
Manual assessment of whether executing the generated SQL produces the expected benchmark result.
<br>

<b>Valid Execution Score (VES)</b><br>
Execution-efficiency metric derived from end-to-end benchmark execution timing and used to compare performance across models and database configurations.
</div>
</details>


<details>
<summary><b>📊 Analysis & Reporting (analysis/)</b></summary>
<br>
<div class="box">
The <code>analysis/</code> folder contains the validated analytical outputs, statistical results and reporting artefacts generated by the benchmark pipeline. It forms the bridge between benchmark execution and research conclusions.

Unlike the <code>scripts/</code> folder, which orchestrates the evaluation workflow, the <code>analysis/</code> folder stores the datasets, reports and visualisations that support interpretation, comparison and reporting of benchmark results.

The analysis workflow operates on benchmark artefacts stored under <code>data/</code>, including raw benchmark captures, evaluation templates, manually scored datasets and validated analytical outputs.
<br>
<br>

<b>Analytical Workflow</b>
<br>

Raw Benchmark Data<br>
↓<br>
Evaluation Templates<br>
↓<br>
Manual EM / EX Scoring<br>
↓<br>
Execution-Level Dataset<br>
↓<br>
Question-Level Analysis<br>
↓<br>
Question-Type Analysis<br>
↓<br>
Dataset Validation<br>
↓<br>
Statistical Analysis<br>
↓<br>
Visual Reporting
<br>

<br>
<b>Scored Datasets</b>
<br>
Scripts:
<code>33_prepare_evaluation_data.R</code>,
<code>34_analyse_evaluation.R</code>
<br>

Purpose:
Preserve manually assigned EM and EX evaluations while maintaining a clear separation between machine-generated benchmark observations and human-generated assessment results.
<br>

<b>Validated Analytical Outputs</b>
<br>
Scripts:
<code>34_analyse_evaluation.R</code>,
<code>35_analyse_performance.R</code>,
<code>36_A_master_dataset_verification.R</code>,
<code>37_A_*</code>,
<code>39_A_*</code>
<br>

Purpose:
Store trusted execution-level datasets, aggregated performance summaries, validation reports and statistical test results used throughout the research process.
<br>

<b>Visual Reporting</b>
<br>
Scripts:
<code>36_B_visualise_EM_EX.R</code>,
<code>36_C_visualise_EM_EX_per_model.R</code>,
<code>37_B_EX_performance_and_significance.R</code>,
<code>38_A_VES_overall.R</code>,
<code>38_B_VES_per_model.R</code>,
<code>39_B_VES_performance_and_significance.R</code>,
<code>40_A_SQL_generation_quality.R</code>
<br>

Purpose:
Provide publication-ready visualisations for:
- Exact Match (EM)
- Execution Match (EX)
- Valid Execution Score (VES)
- SQL generation quality

Visualisations support:
- model comparisons;
- database-mode comparisons;
- performance interpretation;
- statistical significance reporting.
<br>

<b>Research Outputs</b>
<br>
The artefacts generated within this folder provide the evidence base used to evaluate LLM behaviour, compare database configurations and report benchmark findings.
</div>
</details>


<details>
<summary><b>✅ Quality Assurance & Validation (utils/)</b></summary>
<br>
<div class="box">
The <code>utils/</code> folder contains diagnostic and validation scripts used to verify that the application, database configuration and execution pipeline behave as expected before benchmark experiments are performed.
<br>

<br>
<b>Infrastructure Validation</b>
<br>
- <code>100_checks_db_connection.R</code>
  - Validates database connectivity and schema accessibility.

- <code>110_check_full_gdb_relationships.R</code>
  - Validates Full-GDB table relationships and referential integrity.

- <code>200_check_ollama_config.R</code>
  - Validates Ollama connectivity and model availability.

<br>
<b>Pipeline Validation</b>
<br>
- <code>300_check_query_execution.R</code>
  - Validates end-to-end Natural Language → SQL → Database execution.

- <code>400_check_logging_pipeline.R</code>
  - Validates execution logging, timing capture and metadata collection.

<br>
<b>Application Validation</b>
<br>
- <code>500_check_shiny_ui.R</code>
  - Validates Shiny user-interface components and layout.

- <code>600_check_shiny_server.R</code>
  - Validates server-side integration and application workflow.

# 🔁 Reproducibility

<div class="box">
Reproducibility is a core design principle of the RVAT NLQ project. Application behaviour, benchmark executions and analytical results can be reproduced across development, research and deployment environments.
<br>

<b>Version Control</b>
<br>
- GitHub manages source-code, benchmark and documentation changes.
- Repository history provides traceability for application and research developments.
<br>

<b>Environment Management</b>
<br>
- <code>renv</code> maintains a reproducible R environment.
- Package versions are captured in <code>renv.lock</code>.
- <code>.Rprofile</code> automatically activates the project environment.
<br>

Restore the environment:
```r
renv::restore()
